researched_by: the Authority's own visitor and community pages, cross-checked against Forestry England's New Forest parking pages, the Verderers' byelaws and New Forest District Council's off-street parking order
policy_summary:
The New Forest National Park Authority has no overnight instrument of its own, because it has almost nothing to apply one to. Its own car parking page says it plainly: 'The National Park Authority doesn't own or manage any car parks.' The car parks in the National Park belong to somebody else - over 130 to Forestry England on the open Forest, more than 50 to New Forest District Council in the towns and on the coast, four to the National Trust and two to Hampshire County Council. The Authority is a planning authority and an advocacy body. It makes no off-street parking order, it is not the highway authority, and it holds no land on which a byelaw could bite.

What it does publish is a statement of everyone else's rules: 'Wild camping is not allowed in the New Forest, nor overnight stays in car parks.' That is accurate but it is not the Authority's own prohibition. The instruments that actually stop a van sleeping in the New Forest are Forestry England's - its New Forest car parks are open 04:00 to 23:00 only and 'anyone failing to pay for parking or parking during 11:00pm to 4:00am when the car parks are closed may be liable to a parking charge notice' - and New Forest District Council's, whose Off Street Parking Places Order 2005 bans sleeping or camping in any vehicle in any of its car parks (see new-forest-district.json).

On verges the Authority is the loudest voice and the weakest hand. It tells visitors 'Do not park on the verge or block gateways' and explains why: the verges are not ordinary grass, they are 'protected habitats in their own right', designated SSSI on Crown land and the adjacent commons, and the gateways are needed at all times by commoners tending stock and by emergency vehicles. Enforcement is somebody else's - 'Forestry England staff, NPA rangers and the Police are working together to address issues as they arise'. NPA rangers can ask; only the landowner and the police can compel.

Grazing is a third jurisdiction again. The commoners' stock that make the verge question matter are regulated by the Verderers of the New Forest, a separate statutory body under the New Forest Act 1877 with its own byelaws: byelaw 4 stops any animal being depastured unless entitled, byelaws 6 and 7 require marking fees, and byelaw 17(1) makes it an offence for anyone other than the owner, an authorised agent or an agister to hand feed a New Forest pony, cow, pig or sheep. Penalty is a fine at level 1 on the standard scale. The Authority repeats it as advice - 'Keep your distance from the animals and don't feed or pet them - you may be fined' - but the byelaw is the Verderers'.

Direction of travel: the pressure point in 2026 is displacement. Forestry England began charging for New Forest car parking on 20 April 2026 at GBP1.50 for an hour rising to GBP8 for over four hours, and the New Forest Association, with the New Forest Dog Owners Group, has started a 'Verge Watch' precisely because it expects the charges to push vehicles onto the verges the Authority spends its time defending. The Authority has recruited volunteer ambassadors to record verge and gateway parking. It is monitoring a problem it cannot legally fix.

notes:
This file is deliberately empty of sites, and that is the finding rather than a gap. The New Forest is the clearest case in the dataset of a national park authority with no estate: it owns no car parks, has made no byelaw, holds no traffic powers, and has published no overnight motorhome policy of its own. Everything a van user would actually be penalised for in the New Forest comes from Forestry England, New Forest District Council or Hampshire County Council. Recording the Authority as 'no provision, no restriction' is honest; recording other bodies' rules against its name would be wrong and would double-count the same prohibition three times over.

The one lever the Authority genuinely holds is planning. Any new aire, stopover or campsite inside the National Park boundary needs its consent, and National Park purposes make that a high bar. If provision ever appears in the New Forest it will be because the Authority permitted it, not because it built it - so this file is worth re-checking whenever Forestry England or the District Council float a stopover scheme.

Worth carrying forward: Forestry England's national 'Forest Campervan Road Trip' scheme has seven locations and none of them is in the New Forest, despite the New Forest being its single busiest forest. That is a policy choice, not an oversight, and it is consistent with the flat line taken by every body here - somewhere else, not here.

Caution on the sources: newforestnpa.gov.uk is the Authority; new-forest-national-park.com is a commercial visitor site that reproduces the Verderers' byelaws. The byelaw text used here came from the latter and should be checked against the Verderers' own publication before anything is asserted about penalties.

PROVISION THE PARKING PAGES DO NOT MENTION - CHECKED, NONE FOUND (27 July 2026). Because the Authority owns no car parks, the obvious next question is whether it owns anything else you can sleep on, and it was checked separately: country parks, council campsites and caravan sites, marinas and harbours, and any site let to an operator. The Authority runs none. It has no country park, no campsite, no caravan or touring site, no holiday park, no marina and no harbour, and as a 2005 creation it inherited no district caravan site from anyone.

Every overnight site inside the National Park boundary belongs to someone else. The ten forest campsites - Ashurst, Hollands Wood, Denny Wood, Matley Wood, Ocknell, Longbeech, Roundhill, Setthorns, Aldridge Hill and Holmsley - are FORESTRY ENGLAND's, run as Camping in the Forest on Crown land, and are emphatically not the Authority's; Forestry England also owns the forest car parks and is introducing charges at them. The one public campsite in the National Park that takes caravans and motorhomes is HAMPSHIRE COUNTY COUNCIL's at Calshot Activities Centre on Calshot Spit, recorded in hampshire-county-council.json, and Hampshire also runs Tile Barn Outdoor Centre at Brockenhurst and Minstead Study Centre. Lepe Country Park, also inside the boundary, is Hampshire's too and is a restriction, not provision. Everything else is private or club supply.

The file's conclusion is unchanged and now rests on both halves of the check rather than one: this Authority holds no land a van can stay on and no instrument it could use to allow or forbid it. Its only lever remains planning.
open_questions: Does the New Forest National Park Local Plan carry a specific policy on touring caravan, campervan or campsite development? The Authority's planning policy pages could not be fetched this session (blocked), so the policy number and wording are unrecorded.
Has the Authority ever made byelaws under section 90 of the National Parks and Access to the Countryside Act 1949? Nothing found suggests it has, but absence was not positively confirmed.
What has Verge Watch actually recorded since Forestry England's charges started on 20 April 2026? The displacement question is the live one and the data would be the first hard evidence either way.

Which two car parks in the National Park belong to Hampshire County Council, and do they carry overnight restrictions? Hampshire County Council needs its own file - it is the highway authority for the whole district and it made the Keyhaven on-street motorhome ban.
